Ecological regression with expected counts

Source: R/sep.R
ecolrg.Rd

Regression of area counts y on covariates with the offset log(e), e the expected counts (from indirect standardisation, say), so that the coefficients act on the standardised ratio: Poisson by iteratively reweighted least squares; negative binomial, alternating Newton steps on the score of theta with reweighted fits of the coefficients; or zero-inflated Poisson (Lambert 1992) by EM, the zero part logistic on an intercept and the columns of z.

Usage

ecolrg(y, e, x = NULL, family = "poisson", z = NULL, tol = 1e-12, maxit = 500)

Arguments

y

The counts: numbers from 0.

e

The expected counts: positive numbers, one per count.

x

NULL, or the covariates: a numeric matrix (or vector) with one row per count. An intercept is added.

family

"poisson", "negbin" or "zip".

z

For "zip": NULL, or the covariates of the zero part, as x.

tol

The convergence tolerance of theta and of the zero-inflated log-likelihood: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

maxit

The rounds: one whole number from 1.

Value

A list of class ecolrg: coef (the intercept first), theta (negative binomial), zcoef (zero-inflated), fitted (the means of the count part) and loglik.

References

Lambert, D. (1992). Zero-inflated Poisson regression, with an application to defects in manufacturing. Technometrics, 34(1), 1-14. doi:10.2307/1269547

Lawson, A. B. (2018). Bayesian Disease Mapping, third edition. Chapman and Hall/CRC, Boca Raton. doi:10.1201/9781351271769

See also

Other spatial epidemiology: bayout(), bufexp(), bym2sc(), evfilt(), kerexp(), lerprc(), sfrail(), spbias(), spsir()

Examples

# simulated counts and expected counts
set.seed(1)
x <- rnorm(30)
e <- runif(30, 3, 8)
y <- rpois(30, e * exp(0.2 + 0.4 * x))
ecolrg(y, e, x)
#> ecolrg: 30 counts, log-likelihood -67.3106
#> [1] 0.1404659 0.4851843
